deep.reconstruction:
This page sits inside a 1953 manuscript on majorization inequalities. Their purpose is to compare the eigenvalues λ_i of an operator u on a Hilbert space with its singular values (s-numbers) ρ_i. This is the machinery behind the Weyl inequalities that Grothendieck used for Fredholm determinants and for nuclear/p-summing operators.

The preceding page proves a lemma by Abel summation (formula (9)). If α_1≥…≥α_n and the partial sums satisfy α_1+…+α_m ≤ β_1+…+β_m (weak majorization, 'hypothesis a'), or the same with equality at m=n ('hypothesis b'), then Σ a_iα_i ≤ Σ a_iβ_i for decreasing a_i ≥ 0. From this follows φ(α) ≤ φ(β) for suitable convex φ. As a corollary, (10) gives f(1/σ_i) ≤ f(1/ρ_i).

This page:
(i) A first attempt is crossed out: the 'negative' version Σφ(−α) ≤ Σφ(β).
(ii) Remarque 1. If (α_i)_{i≤n} and (β_i)_{i≤n} satisfy the partial-sum conditions, then so do the truncated sequences (α_i)_{i≤k} and (β_i)_{i≤k} for every 1≤k≤n. The lemma therefore also gives φ(α_1,…,α_k) ≤ φ(β_1,…,β_k) for every k. This is the passage from a single inequality to the family of all its 'Ky Fan k-truncations' needed in Th. 1, 2°.
(iii) Examples of functions f satisfying the hypotheses of Th. 1, 2°. The criterion is that f(e^{t_1},…,e^{t_n}) be a convex function of (t_i) ∈ R^n, i.e. f is 'geometrically convex'. Examples given:
- functions Σ a_i r_i + b with a_i ≥ 0, for which f(e^t) = Σ a_i e^{t_i} + b is convex since each e^{t_i} is convex and the coefficients are nonnegative;
- symmetric norms N on R^n with N(x) = N(|x_1|,…,|x_n|), i.e. symmetric gauge functions (von Neumann).
(iv) Remarque 2 in the margin (rotated). If f(α) ≤ f(β) holds whenever Σ_{i≤k}α_i ≤ Σ_{i≤k}β_i, the same applies to N.

The next page draws the consequences:
- Σρ_i^p ≤ Σσ_i^p under log-majorization (15)–(16);
- N(ρ) ≤ N(σ) (11)–(12);
- the 'convexity theorem in Hilbert space' (17): f(|λ_1|,…,|λ_n|) ≤ f(ρ_1,…,ρ_n) for every continuous symmetric f with f(e^t) convex.

In modern terms: weak log-majorization of the eigenvalue moduli by the singular values (Weyl–Horn) implies f(|λ|) ≤ f(s) for every increasing, symmetric, geometrically convex f.
errors: For weak (log-)majorization (hypothesis a), convexity of f(e^t) alone is not sufficient. One also needs f increasing in each variable, or equality of total products (hypothesis b). The page does not state monotonicity explicitly in the examples. It is automatic for the linear examples with a_i ≥ 0 and for absolute (symmetric) norms, so the examples are fine but the general criterion as written is incomplete.

Σ a_i r_i + b is symmetric only if all a_i are equal. If symmetry is required in Th. 1, 2°, the example as stated is too broad, although harmless since the Abel-summation argument uses ordered sequences.
The first transcribed hypothesis reads 't_i > 0', but the correct domain for (t_i) is all of R^n, i.e. r_i = e^{t_i} > 0. Grothendieck corrects this himself in the next line.

ideas.what: Abel-summation proof that prefix-sum (weak) majorization implies inequalities for convex/increasing functions, together with the observation that truncations inherit the hypotheses
ideas.where_published: Possibly used implicitly in 'La théorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 1956) and in 'Produits tensoriels topologiques' (Memoirs AMS 1955)

ideas.what: Functions f with f(e^{t_1},…,e^{t_n}) convex as the right class for eigenvalue–singular-value comparison
ideas.modern_name: Geometrically convex (log-convex-in-exponential), Schur-convex functions; weak log-majorization
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Weyl (1949), A. Horn (1950), Ky Fan (1951), Ostrowski (1952), later Marshall–Olkin
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'La théorie de Fredholm' (1956) uses Σ|λ_i|^p ≤ Σ s_i^p; general f-version unsure

ideas.what: Symmetric norms N with N(x)=N(|x|) satisfy the hypotheses, hence N(|λ|) ≤ N(s)
ideas.modern_name: Symmetric gauge functions / unitarily invariant norms; Ky Fan dominance

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard working-out of Weyl/Ky Fan majorization inequalities (1949–1951) for use in Grothendieck's operator-ideal and Fredholm work. Nothing here goes beyond what Weyl, Horn, Ky Fan and Ostrowski had published by 1952. It is historically interesting only as evidence of Grothendieck reproving these tools himself in 1953.
transcription_corrections: The heading on the left margin is 'Remarque 1' (written vertically/aside), and a separate rotated marginal note headed 'Remarque 2' appears at lower left.
'l'ensemble des arguments t_i > 0' should be read as the set of positive arguments r_i > 0, with the convexity condition then stated for (t_i) ∈ R^n.
The final displayed condition reads N(x_1,…,x_n) = N(|x_1|,…,|x_n|), with an inserted note 'pour x_1 ≥ … ≥ x_n ≥ 0'. A crossed-out normalization 'N(e_i)=1' follows.
